channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro: France spreads weigh on EUR – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING sees EUR/USD downside risks persisting, with the 1.1320–1.1330 area as key support that could be tested quickly on stronger US data or another sharp Oil move higher.

item.title: US Dollar: Rate differentials support but upside constrained – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the recent pullback in Oil prices has eased global bond selling and cooled the Dollar rally.

item.title: Indian Rupee gets cushioned by RBI’s likely intervention on Friday
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains a temporary ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday after remaining under pressure in the past few days. The USD/INR pair struggles to extend gains above 95.96 on the likely Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) intervention.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD reclaims $65 as rally in bond yields, US Dollar hits pause
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is up 1.85% to near $65.00 during the European trading session on Friday. The white metal strengthens as rally in the US Dollar (USD) and United States (US) Treasury Yields appears to have hit a pause.

item.title: British Pound: Risk of test of 1.3140 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that GBP/USD extended its sharp decline to 1.3205, leaving conditions deeply oversold but with the bias still pointing lower.

item.title: Gold gains as US Dollar and yields pause, but weekly loss remains in sight
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges higher on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) and Treasury yields take a breather following their strong rally this week. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,310 after slipping to a one-week low of $4,244 on Thursday.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: Persistent supply shocks cannot be ignored
item.description: New York Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank John Willams said in a panel discussion at Oxford University on Friday that although tariffs and higher energy prices don’t to a sustainable inflation. However, repeated supply shocks are keeping price pressures higher.

item.title: WTI Oil reversal stalls above $91.00 as Middle East tensions outweigh supply increases
item.description: The price of the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel has stabilised above $91.00 on Friday, with the reversal from Thursday’s highs, near $96.00, losing momentum.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama: Takaichi very much respects the independence of the BoJ
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama stresses on Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) independence while speaking during the European trading session on Friday. This is the second time in the day when Katayama has delivered remarks on economy and currency.

item.title: BoE’s Bailey warns persistent high energy prices could challenge rate stance
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Governor Andrew Bailey said on Friday that the pass-through from higher energy prices remains “quite subdued” so far, while stressing that it is still early days.

item.title: Indian Rupee: PMIs show growth and inflation risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s India section notes September flash PMIs pointing to stronger end-Q3 activity, with both manufacturing and services indices well above 50. Domestic demand is robust, but elevated input and output prices, especially in manufacturing, keep upside inflation risks high.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD struggles below $4,300 level with bears still in control
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) is trimming some losses on Friday, trading just below the $4,300 level after bouncing from support in the $4,230 area on Thursday.

item.title: Brent: conflict-driven gains face deal hopes – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight a sharp rise in Brent Oil as geopolitical tensions and Iranian rhetoric fuel concerns about an extended conflict. Brent briefly spiked above $108 before retracing on reports of potential US–Iran negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $64.60 per troy ounce, up 1.18% from the $63.85 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Still a low-yield funding currency – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that the Swiss National Bank (SNB) kept rates at 0% and toned down its FX intervention language, signalling more tolerance for a firmer Swiss Franc but not a hawkish shift.

item.title: Euro: Downside scope seen limited against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that EUR/USD extended its recent slide to 1.1358, leaving conditions deeply oversold.

item.title: British Pound trades lower against Japanese Yen amid intervention fears
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) recovers some of its early losses against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Friday, but is still down around 0.17% to near 209.45.

item.title: CEE FX: Energy shock lifts tightening bets – ING
item.description: ING strategist Frantisek Taborsky reports that volatility in core rates and high Oil and gas prices are driving elevated tightening expectations across CEE, with roughly 125bp priced for Poland and the Czech Republic.

item.title: Australian Dollar hovers just above 0.7000 with no news from the Trump-Xi summit
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) ticks up against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday but remains on track to a 1.3% weekly decline, to complete a three-week losing streak.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: New inflation target demands hawkish MNB – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes the National Bank of Hungary paused cuts at 5.50% but lowered its medium‑term inflation target to 2.5% while simultaneously lifting 2027 inflation forecasts.

item.title: Bank of England: Policy convergence questions after Fed hike – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Christopher Graham examines whether the Bank of England will feel pressured to follow the Federal Reserve’s September rate hike. He notes that Fed tightening alone does not force the BoE to act and stresses the role of UK data and market credibility.

item.title: British Pound underperforms this week as experts doubt BoE tightening prospects
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) trades with caution against its major currency peers on Friday. Against the US Dollar (USD), it is marginally up at around 1.3220 during the European session, but is close to its almost three-month low of 1.3200.

item.title: Euro consolidates near three-month lows amid high Oil prices, Fed hiking bets
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains practically flat against the US Dollar on Friday, trading within a tight range around 1.1380, after dropping 0.8% this week and nearly 2% over the last two weeks.

item.title: Gold extends the range play below $4,300 as Fed hike bets counter modest USD pullback
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to gain any traction and remains confined in a narrow range near the weekly low through the early European session on Friday amid a bearish fundamental backdrop.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar inches higher as US Dollar declines on easing bond yields
item.description: NZD/USD holds gains after experiencing volatility, trading around 0.5660 during European hours on Friday. The currency pair holds gains as the US Dollar (USD) struggles despite market caution amid persistent hawkish sentiment surrounding the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy outlook.

item.title: Gold: Bearish bias holds below 4300 resistance - OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that Gold remains under near-term pressure after briefly slipping below 4250 before rebounding modestly.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar consolidates weekly gains ahead of mid-tier data
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Friday, September 25:

item.title: Dow Jones futures rise as treasury yields, oil prices ease
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain by 0.14% to trade near 51,790 during European hours on Friday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures rise by 0.33% to trade around 7,780, while Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.34% to trade near 30,870.

item.title: Equities: Rising yields weigh on stocks despite tech support - Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists report renewed pressure on global equities as surging bond yields and higher Oil prices weigh on risk assets. The S&P 500 slipped for a third session despite a late recovery, while European indices saw broader declines.

item.title: Euro hovers near three-month highs against British Pound despite weak German data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains practically flat, just below three-month highs against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, despite the downbeat German consumer confidence data released earlier in the day.
